content: popstate only fires on back/forward, not on pushState/replaceState, which is what SPA routers (including x.com) use for in-app navigation -- so content scripts cannot rely on popstate alone. Three standard solutions: (1) monkey-patch history.pushState/replaceState in the page context to dispatch a custom event on every call (must run in MAIN world or via injected script since patching in ISOLATED world only affects the isolated copy of history in Chrome... actually history object is shared, so ISOLATED-world patching of window.history.pushState does work in Chrome content scripts since DOM/BOM objects are shared while JS heap is isolated); (2) the new Navigation API (window.navigation, 'navigate' event, Chrome 102+) which fires for all navigation types including pushState-driven ones -- simplest and most reliable where available; (3) chrome.webNavigation.onHistoryStateUpdated from the background/service worker, which requires the webNavigation permission and message-passes into the content script. Polling window.location.href via setInterval works but wastes CPU and adds latency.
